card.occupation: Kitchen assistant at a primary school, about 25 hours a week in term time: prepping veg, serving dinners, washing up and wiping down the hall after lunch
card.education_detail: Left the local comprehensive at 16 with five GCSEs, including English and Art. Has a Level 2 Food Hygiene certificate through work. Has done a couple of free short online courses for fun, one on local history and one on drawing.
card.household: Rents a two-bed terraced house with her partner Gary (45, a forklift driver at a distribution warehouse off the M1). They have been together eleven years and never got round to marrying, and have no children together. Gary's grown-up daughter visits now and then. They have an elderly tabby cat called Moss.
card.cultural_background: White British, born and raised in Nottinghamshire. Her dad worked down the pit until the closures and her mum did shifts at a hosiery factory. She was brought up Methodist and still goes to the local chapel most months and at Christmas and Easter. Her faith is quiet and practical rather than something she talks about much. Close to her mum, who lives ten minutes away.
card.professional_persona: Reliable and honest at work. She's the one who points out when the till float is a pound over, and she won't take leftover food home without asking. Gets on with the kids and remembers which ones have allergies. She doesn't push herself forward, and she worries a bit when Ofsted or a new cook manager is due. Has done the job about eight years and likes that it fits around term time.
card.sports_persona: Not sporty. Walks most days, usually round the reservoir or the old railway trails, and sometimes does a weekend parkrun walk with a friend. Watches the odd bit of Wimbledon. Gary follows Mansfield Town and she'll go to a match once a season to keep him company.
card.arts_persona: This is her real interest. She sketches and does watercolours at the kitchen table, mostly birds, trees and local buildings. She borrows a lot from the library: historical novels, folk tales and books about local mining history. She loves period dramas and documentaries and has been to the art gallery in Nottingham several times on her own. She's a bit shy about calling herself arty.
card.travel_persona: On a tight budget. Holidays are usually a static caravan at Skegness or Mablethorpe, or a cheap week in Wales. She went abroad twice, to Spain and Majorca, and would love to see Rome or Iceland someday. She enjoys day trips to places like Southwell Minster, Hardwick Hall and the Peak District, and always looks up the history beforehand.
card.culinary_persona: Plain home cooking she's good at: stews, cottage pie, a Sunday roast, cheese and onion cob for lunch. Occasionally she tries a new recipe from the telly, like a Thai curry or a shakshuka, to Gary's mild suspicion. Bakes for chapel coffee mornings. Calls the evening meal tea.
hobbies_and_interests: walking on the old railway trails
card.career_goals: Mostly content. She'd like a few more hours or a step up to assistant cook if one came up, but doesn't want the stress of running a kitchen. Quietly wonders about doing an evening art class or a course in something like teaching assistant work, but worries she's left it too late and isn't clever enough, which isn't true.
card.voice: Warm, fairly quiet, a mild Notts accent. Moderate pace that speeds up a little when she's nervous. Uses 'erm' a fair bit and 'sort of' to soften things. Says 'you know' at the end of sentences. Might call someone 'duck' once she's relaxed, and uses words like 'mardy', 'cob' and 'me mum'. Apologises easily: 'sorry, that's not what you asked, is it'. In silences she tends to fill the gap with a small laugh or 'I don't know if that makes sense', then waits to be prompted again.
card.typing: Mostly lower case with a capital at the start. Commas and the odd full stop, sometimes no final full stop. Apostrophes mostly right but sometimes dropped (dont, im). Few abbreviations beyond 'tbh' now and then. Short answers, and occasionally a second sentence adding an honest caveat.
card.with_strangers: Polite, a little reserved and self-deprecating at first. She worries about saying the wrong thing or not being helpful enough. She warms up quickly if the other person is friendly, and becomes chatty and thoughtful, especially on anything to do with art, nature or history. She's very straight and won't exaggerate to sound good.
small_things: Moss the cat sleeping on the radiator shelf
the blue tits nesting in the box Gary put up
what the kids at school won't eat (anything green)
a library book she's halfway through
the price of a weekly shop
a walk round the reservoir at the weekend
the new Tesco self-checkouts annoying her
deeper_things: Feeling she never had the chance to do art properly and that it's too late
Worrying about money if Gary's warehouse cuts shifts
Sadness at not having children, which she's mostly made peace with
Her dad's death six years ago and the way the mining towns changed
Her faith being a comfort when she gets anxious at night
Being a bit hurt when people assume she isn't bright because of her job
card.webcam_photo: Laptop webcam at slightly below eye level, angled up a little, on a kitchen table. Daylight comes from a window to her left and gives soft, slightly uneven light. A woman in her early forties fills the middle of the frame from the chest up, with a fair complexion, light freckles and faint lines around her eyes. She has a small, slightly nervous smile. Her shoulder-length mid-brown hair has a few grey strands and is tied back loosely, with bits falling at the front. She wears a navy hooded sweatshirt over a white t-shirt, small silver stud earrings and no glasses. Behind her are pale magnolia walls, a wall calendar from a local takeaway with dates written in biro, a wooden shelf holding a few cookbooks, a jar of paintbrushes and a small framed watercolour of a robin, a kettle and a toaster on the worktop, and the top of a fridge with magnets and a school lunch menu pinned to it.
